extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of English poetry; literary critics and teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and critical standards for evaluating English poets and their works (satire, comic writing, odes, elegies, prose letters) as discussed in a lecture-format literary-criticism text. Emphasises qualities like wit, invention, moral purpose, style, and lasting effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of character and costume
rubrics_metrics.description: The preservation of the character and costume is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity in depicting social role and outward detail (example: Polly describing her lover going to the gallows with touching simplicity; even butchers weep and Jack Ketch refuses his fee). A faithful, convincing portrayal of character and milieu enhances comic and moral effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of gaiety and imagination to humanize subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet has thrown all the gaiety and sunshine of the imagination... round the short-lived existence of his heroes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employing bright imagination and pleasure to portray characters makes satire 'good-natured but instructive' and can soften harsher judgments; wit can 'take off from the offensiveness of the satire' so readers (even targeted statesmen) may enjoy it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of moral/theme (didactic aim)
rubrics_metrics.description: The moral of the piece is to shew the vulgarity of vice; same violations of integrity and decorum are common to the great and the mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, convincing moral or theme—here, exposing universal vice—strengthens satirical works when characters' arguments convincingly show the point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sparkling wit and keen sarcasm
rubrics_metrics.description: Every line in this sterling comedy sparkles with wit, and is fraught with the keenest sarcasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent verbal brilliance and sarcasm are virtues; they energise the work and can mitigate offensiveness, inviting readers to laugh rather than resent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire that detects disguises rank lends to vice
rubrics_metrics.description: Detected the disguises which rank and circumstances lend to exalted vice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good satire not only indicts low vice but exposes how social rank masks the same faults—demonstrating universality of hypocrisy strengthens moral critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of invention (conception) vs execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the excellence of Gulliver's Travels is in the conception or the execution... the power is somewhere, and it is a power that has moved the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss a work because critics find execution mechanical; originality of conception can carry a work's greatness. Evaluate both invention and execution, but acknowledge that transformative ideas may outweigh mechanical shortcomings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accessibility of satirical conceit
rubrics_metrics.description: He enlarges or diminishes the scale, as he wishes to shew the insignificance or the grossness of our over-weening self-love... comes equally home to the understanding of the man and of the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical devices should be precise, well‑kept, and intelligible across audiences; mathematically precise conceits (e.g., changes of scale) that are clear to both lay and learned readers are strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual method to achieve moral effect
rubrics_metrics.description: To strip empty pride and grandeur of the imposing air which external circumstances throw around them; reduce every thing to the abstract predicament of size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a consistent conceptual approach (metaphor, scale, inverse perspective) that reinforces the moral aim—technique should serve the thesis of the poem/prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incisiveness and abruptness in separating truth from folly
rubrics_metrics.description: He separates, with a severe and caustic air, truth from falsehood, folly from wisdom... the force, the precision, and the honest abruptness with which the separation is made, that excites our surprise, our admiration, and laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Powerful satire uses sharp, precise contrasts and abrupt moral marks of reprobation; clarity and force in exposure elicit both admiration and comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic invention suited to voice/character
rubrics_metrics.description: He has gone so far as to invent a new stanza of fourteen and sixteen syllable lines for Mary the cookmaid to vent her budget of nothings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal or metrical innovations are praiseworthy when they fit the speaker's character and purpose; invention in stanza or voice can enhance verisimilitude and humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend of dry humour, irony and pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not only a dry humour, an exquisite tone of irony, in these productions... but there is a touching, unpretending pathos, mixed up with the most whimsical and eccentric strokes of pleasantry and satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful mix of irony and genuine pathos deepens moral and emotional resonance; balancing comic eccentricity with touching feeling strengthens a poet's rank as 'agreeable moralist'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate comedic tone (serious, fantastical, or sportive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Swift's wit... was serious, saturnine, and practical; Rabelais' was fantastical and joyous; Voltaire's was light, sportive, and verbal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tonal quality of wit to authorial purpose: saturnine seriousness suits moral sting; joyous extravagance suits exuberant nonsense; light verbal wit suits delicate irony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy, subtlety and tact in satirical attack
rubrics_metrics.description: He expresses his contempt by the most indirect hints, and in the fewest words... The poisoned wound he inflicted was so fine, as scarcely to be felt till it rankled and festered in its mortal consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtle, economical insults can be more effective than noisy invective; the finest satire wounds slowly and endures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion and sustained execution matching moral
rubrics_metrics.description: Candide... is in the most perfect keeping, and without any appearance of effort. Every sentence tells, and the whole reads like one sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency of tone and tight execution that serve the stated moral strengthen a work—cohesion makes each line contribute to the overall argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint in moralizing (avoid overloading attention)
rubrics_metrics.description: His Universal Passion is a keen and powerful satire; but the effort takes from the effect, and oppresses attention by perpetual and violent demands upon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive, relentless moral emphasis can fatigue readers and weaken impact; moderation and variation keep attention and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lasting emotional residue (stings that never wear out)
rubrics_metrics.description: He leaves stings in the minds of his readers, certain traces of thought and feelings which never wear out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure poetic success by the work's ability to persist in the reader's mind—lasting images, phrases, or ideas indicate genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine 'vivida vis' / inspired imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: That true vivida vis, that genuine inspiration, which alone can give birth to the highest efforts of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A distinct, intense imaginative power is required for the greatest poetry; occasional affectation or obscurity can be forgiven if true inspiration is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attic simplicity, pathos, and fervour of imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: In his best works there is an attic simplicity, a pathos, and fervour of imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refinement and unobtrusive simplicity coupled with heartfelt feeling and imaginative reach are marks of high lyric quality (example: Collins' best work, Gray's ode passages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal moral resonance (classical moralising)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elegy in a Country Church-yard: one of the most classical productions... moralising on human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems that thoughtfully moralise on shared human conditions with a classical tone (elegiac gravity) attain lasting status; language should remain intelligible to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness and freedom from affectation in prose
rubrics_metrics.description: His prose is quite free from affectation. He pours his thoughts out upon paper as they arise in his mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prose that reads as spontaneous and unpretentious is praiseworthy; avoid 'stilts' and buckram—authentic voice matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of imitation and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: His genius was a mixture of originality and imitation: he could do nothing without some model before him, and he could copy nothing that he did not adorn with the graces of his own mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good writers may borrow models but must transform them with individual grace; originality within imitation is a critical virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of comic characterisation
rubrics_metrics.description: As a comic writer, his Tony Lumpkin draws forth new powers from Mr. Liston's face. That alone is praise enough for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic writing should create characters and situations that produce immediate, observable comic effect—measured by audience reaction or performative success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of careful revision and pruning
rubrics_metrics.description: He improved his Pleasures of the Imagination in the subsequent editions, by pruning away a great many redundances of style and ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editing out redundancies and over-ornamentation improves poetic effect; later editions that prune excesses are often stronger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for occasional verse and institutional duties
rubrics_metrics.description: He bore his honours meekly, and performed his half-yearly task regularly. (poet-laureate duties)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to write competent occasional verse and fulfill formal poetic roles is a recognised (if not primary) skill in a poet's oeuvre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of short forms (sonnet craft)
rubrics_metrics.description: He is the author of some of the finest sonnets in the language... this species of composition has the necessary advantage of being short.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill in compact forms (sonnets) — treating pleasing subjects philosophically and with concision — is a notable poetic merit.
